rationale_overall: This week's pool is dominated by noise rather than genuine new-ticker catalysts. The heaviest volume of articles covers SpaceX's Starship Flight 10 (scrub, delay, then successful launch) — compelling space-wave narrative but SpaceX is privately held with no investable US ticker, so it was discarded entirely. Rocket Lab (RKLB) surfaced with two real, dated, US-listed data points (70th Electron mission success; LC-3 pad inauguration at Wallops), but both are routine operational-cadence news for an already well-known space name rather than a discrete inflection that would justify displacing a core AI/mega-cap holding — not swap-worthy on its own at weekly granularity. Nuclear-wave items (Rolls-Royce SMR IPO denial, Dark Star Minerals uranium talks, Basin Energy uranium/rare-earth deal, China's Hualong One) were all foreign, OTC/CSE/ASX-listed, or government-linked and fail the US-listing/liquidity guardrail. Quantum computing appeared only as a generic trend piece with no ticker attached. Robotics coverage (Nvidia Jetson AGX Thor, Lens Technology, Hyundai Mobis, Reliance Jio robotics push) either concerns an already-held name (NVDA) or foreign-listed companies. Geopolitical/defense items (China military parade, Russia-Ukraine strikes, India/Pakistan rocket command, DRDO Pinaka) are government/military stories with no clean US-listed investable vehicle. Nvidia's own earnings read mixed (H20 China ban hurting revenue vs. continued AI chip sales growth) but this is existing-holding noise, not a removal-grade thesis breach in a single week. Net: watchlist unchanged this period; no clearly stronger rising-wave vehicle displaced an existing holding.
